label: text
text: MR. ATHERLEY AND HIS COMPRADORE.

label: text
text: A PERSONAL MATTER?

label: text
text:
ADVANCESSAND TO BE COMPANY
MONEYS.

label: text
text: For the fourth day, the cross-examination of Mr. Chau,� compradore of Former Getz Bros. Co. (of the Orient Ltd.) continued at the Criminal Sessions proceedings this morning in the case in which Mr. J. E. Atherley is charged with misappropriation.

label: text
text: The issues between the prosecution and the defence were put early to the jury this morning by the Chief Justice.

label: text
text: The Crown says that Mr. Atherley took company money and raised it for his own purposes. Mr. Atherley says, on the other hand that he got these moneys from the compradore (he did not care where the compradore got them) but treated them as a long from the compradore. He treated them as the moneys of the compradore.

label: text
text: Mr. F. C. Jenkin (for the Crown) concurred and Mr. Zeithyn said that he wished he could have put the case as fairly.

label: text
text: A complaint which Mr. Atherley had had from head office in California, with regard to extensions of certain drafts beyond their due date was referred to by Mr. Zeitlyn and Mr. Chau, the compradore, was asked whether it was not a fact that Mr. Atherley talked to him about it.

label: text
text: Witness said he had no recollection of it but at about that time Mr. Atherley asked him about amounts outstanding and from an investigation of the books witness told Mr. Atherley they totalled $70,000. Witness reminded Mr. Atherley that $18,000 of this was money lent to him. Mr. Atherley told him to press for quick payment in respect of the balance.

label: text
text: Witness was cross-examined with regard to what Mr. Zeitlyn termed a change of staff about that time, one of the employees leaving about that time. Witness maintained that there had been no change until the name of the former cashier, Cheung Ho-shi, was put to him. This man had not been dismissed, he said, but had changed from cashier to number two compradore in order that witness, who was poorly at that time, might have assistance.

label: text
text: Witness denied that the cashier left that position because he was $10,000 short in his accounts. He also denied that he told Mr. Atherley any of the office staff were short in their accounts. After this man ceased to be cashier, witness himself made out the deposit slips. The man in question was a nominee of Mr. Wong (witness's own guarantor):

label: paragraph_title
text: Bank Subpena.

label: text
text: At this stage, Mr. Zeitlyn initiated to His Lordship that he made an application that the International Banking Corporation should be called upon to produce the deposit slips of Mr. Atherley's account, the counterfoils of his paying-in book.

label: text
text: His Lordship intimated that the counterfoils did not come under the heading of “bankers books” mentioned in the particular section of the Ordinance referred to. It was a banker's document and he thought the correct thing to do was for Mr. Zeitlyn to subpoena the Bank.

label: text
text: Mr. Zeitlyn agreed and gave it as his case that ever since the arrest of Mr. Atherley on the morning of October 23 in the Hongkong Hotel, the document in question had been in the compradore department of the firm. This had been denied by the compradore.

label: text
text: Mr. Jenkin then re-examined the compradore and indicated that had he been given any idea of the defence he would have made a longer opening and have brought out facts which he would now have to elicit in re-examination.

label: text
text: Mr. Jenkin reminded witness of the interview which took place between Mr. Atherley, Mr. Parkhurst, the Shanghai manager, and Mr. Kelly, of Head Office, California, when the alleged misappropriations were being enquired into. Mr. Parkhurst and Mr. Atherley had gone out to try,

label: paragraph_title
text: INTIMIDATION.

label: text
text: HOTEL PANTRY BOY'S STORY.

label: text
text: TWO CHINESE CHARGED.

label: text
text: A pantry boy employed at the Hongkong Hotel and who remained at his post throughout the strike was the complainant in a case at the Central Magistracy this morning in which two Chinese were charged with alleged intimidation.

label: text
text: the complainant in the course of which he said that the second defendant and four others took him to task for not joining the strikers and demanded a sum of $100 as "forgiveness" money. He had paid over $5 on December 4 and a further $5 a fortnight later, it being agreed that the balance would be paid on January 1. In his dilemma he applied to the compradore for a loan of $50, which he intended to pay over with his month's wages amounting to $40. The compradore, on learning the reason why complainant required the money, reported the matter to Mr. J. P. Bourne, the Hotels Superintendent, and the police were notified.

label: text
text: Further evidence was given that a trap was laid by the police and the two defendants were arrested at the meeting place in a tea-house at Staunton Street on Tuesday afternoon when it had been arranged to pay over $10 as a further installment. Two five dollar notes which changed hands had been marked by the police.

label: text
text: In statements made by the defendants, the first denied knowledge of the affair. He said that he went to have tea at the invitation of the second defendant, a clansman of his, and that the complainant was not known to him. The second defendant, who was a recently engaged worker at the Hotel, claimed that he asked the complainant for a loan of $10, as, owing to the fire, no wages had yet been paid. The complainant invited him to have tea first, and he went to the tea-house together with his clansman. The money was handed to him and soon after he was arrested by detectives who were seated at the tables.

label: text
text: The case was adjourned until Monday.

label: paragraph_title
text: HOME MAIL.

label: text
text: The s.s. "President Lincoln" brought in a heavy mail this morning, the total numbering 376 bags from the U.S.A. and Canada (including Japan and Shanghai). Included in this number were 57 bags from London and 42 bags from the continent despatched via Siberia.

label: text
text: The s.s. "President Grant" with about 406 bags of U.S.A. mail due to-day has been delayed. The vessel is now due at daylight tomorrow.

label: text
text: Mr. Jenkin referred to grave allegations with regard to one of the receipts which had been made in the course of the Criminal Sessions hearing. Mr. Atherley had never before questioned its authenticity, said witness, neither had his solicitors at the two hearings at the magistracy when the document and the others had been produced. The authenticity of the document had never been impugned until these proceedings.

label: text
text: Certain cheques of repayment in respect of money advanced to Mr. Atherley were referred to by Mr. Jenkin. They had been paid into the company's account said witnesses, not his (the compradore's) own account.

label: text
text: Mr. Jenkins initiated that he intended referring later to heavy payments into Mr. Atherley's account other than those specified in the charges. His Lordship at first held against him but Mr. Jenkin indicated that it arose out of Mr. Zeillyn's cross-examination of Mr. Chau with regard to Mr. Atherley's account and His Lords's exp concurred.

label: text
text: FOREIGNERS ROBBED IN YUNNAN.

label: text
text: LOSSES OF TWO LADIES.

label: text
text: (From Our Own Correspondent.)

label: text
text: Yunnanfu, Dec. 23.

label: text
text: A party of foreigners was attacked by bandits on the road to Tilifu. The brigands took from one lady her bedding and other property.

label: text
text: Another old lost her baggage, clothing and effects, to the total value of $3200.

label: text
text: Other brigands captured the city of Kinghui, the centre of the tin mining industry. After exacting tribute of $60,000, the outlaws retired.

label: text
text: Several thousands of troops were sent to deal with them but it is unlikely that a battle will be fought as the brigands have got what they wanted and know when to disappear.

label: text
text: There are many troops apparently idle but little is done to suppress brigandage. Since my last reference to arrears of pay, three months' back money had been promised in settlement but some of the men have not seen the paymaster for fifteen months so that the "squaring up" will only be a drop in the ocean.

label: text
text: On December 18, the Franco-Chinese School was gutted, in spite of all efforts. Only the bare walls are now standing. It was a fierce blaze. When roof fell in the flames, reached 150 feet but neighbouring buildings were not involved as there was hardly any wind.

label: paragraph_title
text: RUBBER CONTROL.

label: text
text: SUGGESTED RETALIATION BY U.S.A.

label: text
text: NOT TAKEN SERIOUSLY.

label: text
text: (Reuter's American Service.)

label: text
text: Washington, Jan. 6.

label: text
text: Although it is not likely to receive serious consideration, it is interesting to record that simultaneously with to-day's opening investigation into British rubber prices, the Democrat, Mr. Tom D. McKeown, in the House of Representatives submitted a proposal for retaliation by increasing the price of American cotton abroad and suggesting the creation of a Commission to regulate the shipment of cotton to the seaports.

label: paragraph_title
text: HOOVER'S DENIAL.

label: text
text: In giving evidence before the House of Representatives Committee which is investigating rubber prices, Mr. Herbert Hoover dwelt on the dangers of the regulation of raw materials by foreign Governments and the arbitrary fixing of prices for all nations.

label: text
text: The United States' experience during the past twelve months was that these controls could no longer be ignored, and a national policy must be determined.

label: text
text:
Mr. Hoover denied that he had been ever thinking that there had been a deliberate attempt to impose on American rubber users. He expressed the opinion that the price of crude rubber had gone much higher than the controllers ever intended.
He added that the raw materials which were at present Governmentally controlled were Egyptian long state cotton, camphor, coffee, iodine, nitrates of potash and mercury rubber, and sisal.

label: text
text: A Chinese woman with a baby slinging on her back produced at the Central Magistracy this morning a photograph of a junk which had once been pirated as proof that her husband was a member of the crew.

label: text
text: The case concerned a small boy who was arrested at Connaught Road West last night and charged with unlawful possession of two tins of milk and a package of Chinese cigarettes. The boy in his statement which he repeated in Court said that the articles were given to him by the seaman to be taken to his family.

label: text
text: With the above proof and a statement made by the boy's mother, the boy was discharged.

label: text
text: A large crowd of ladies, including a number of Chinese, with a sprinkling of some who appeared to be native dressmakers, attended the ladies' department of Messrs. Lane, Crawford's in the Hongkong Hotel, building, this morning, when the stock damaged by water in the New Year Day fire was sold by auction.

label: text
text: Some keen competition was noticed for parasols and other articles for the fair sex.

label: text
text: STRONG REVULSION OF FEELING.

label: text
text: MOVE BY PUBLISHERS.

label: text
text: (Reuter's American Service.)

label: paragraph_title
text: New York, Jan. 6.

label: text
text: The strong revulsion feeling against a coal strike is indicated in a telegram from the publishers of the leading newspapers in the anthracite region to the mine owners' and miners' representatives, who have reached a deadlock at the conference here.

label: text
text: The telegram calls attention to the colossal financial loss, paralysis of business, loss of market for hard coal; and heart-breaking distress that would be caused among the miners.

label: text
text: It adds that the parties' differences regarding arbitration do not justify further division, and the public shall hold the leaders on both sides responsible for the misfortunes of everybody concerned.

label: paragraph_title
text: FENG'S FEARS.

label: text
text: COMING VISIT TO RUSSIA.

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: Tokyo, Jan. 6.

label: text
text: The Foreign Office spokesman, discussing Marshal Feng Yu-hsiang's decision to make a world tour, attached no special significance to his preliminary visit to Russia; but considered the chief reason of this route being taken to be fear of sharing "Little" Hsu's fate if proceeding via Shanghai, Japan, and America.

label: text
text: The Japanese official anticipates that Feng will become the most popular Chinese leader after his return; but expects that Wu Peifu will take advantage of Feng's absence and probably re-appear from his seclusion.

label: text
text: In consequence, it is understood that Government is watching possible developments closely; though it expects that China will be peaceful during the next few months.

label: text
text: With Feng absent and Chang's teeth drawn temporarily, it is considered that Tuan Chi-jui will feel easier in his mind.
